doc.title: John Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Early repertoire: Kenton and Woody Herman records
summary: He recalls the Air Force group playing Stan Kenton and Woody Herman material learned from records the guys brought.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: What we played: tunes and repertoire in the early days

blocks.x: Interesting. What would the, can you recall, at one of those very first gigs you played as a bass player, what were some of the songs that you would have played at the time?
You mean with that Air Force group?
Let’s see. We were into Stan Kenton.
Yeah, I heard a lot of Kenton at that time because the guys would bring their records. And I didn’t listen to jazz or anything like that. I remember “Apple Honey.” [scats] Was that Woody Herman’s?
Yeah, Autumn something. [scats] The saxophones. It was a saxophone thing. And I learned the parts to that by learning to read the parts. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
